editorial.headline: Commercial Sewing and Laundry Machinery, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28261 covers the manufacture of sewing, embroidery, laundry and dry-cleaning machinery, with a sharp Bali caveat for foreign-owned registrations.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28261 is an industrial manufacturing classification for the machines behind garment production, commercial laundry, and dry-cleaning operations. Its scope covers the making of sewing machines, sewing-machine heads, and sewing-machine needles for both household and commercial use, alongside overlock, embroidery, and oversum machines. It also reaches into laundry and dry-cleaning machinery: washing machines with or without water, dryers, ironing machines, and related equipment for penatu and dry-cleaning use.

That makes this a machinery-manufacturing code, not a retail, repair, or laundry-service classification. The centre of gravity is production: building the equipment itself. A founder using this code is describing an activity that manufactures the physical machines used by tailors, garment workshops, laundries, and dry cleaners. The record marks the code as open across the full business scale ladder: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In practical classification terms, it is not confined to one company size; the same activity description can sit behind a small machine workshop or a larger industrial manufacturer, provided the registered activity is the manufacture described in the scope.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clean. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national table treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%. There is no lower foreign-equity cap in the record, and no additional national threshold, licence, or capital figure appears in the slim record. For a national reading of the KBLI alone, this is a foreign-open manufacturing activity.

Bali changes the answer. The Bali-side status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO, and l4_bali_blocked is true. The record’s reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule is also explicit: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest reading is this: KBLI 28261 is nationally open to PMA, but a foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today under the Bali moratorium described in the record. This is not a Bali percentage cap or a partial local-partner rule; the record gives no such figure. It is a Bali registration block tied to the risk-class moratorium, despite the national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 28261 is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, but the record marks it as blocked for PMA registration in Bali today.
